title: EU AI Act Article 2 — Material Scope and Who the Act Applies To (September 2026)
context: 2026-09-01 engine cycle — answer-first seed covering the scope boundary of the EU AI Act; aligned to Council of AI regulatory mapping and the August 2026 application deadline
body: EU AI Act Article 2 defines who the Regulation catches and who walks free. The default rule is broad: any provider placing an AI system on the EU market or putting it into service in the Union, and any deployer of an AI system whose place of establishment or location is in the Union, falls within scope — even if the provider is based outside the EU. The Act reaches extraterritorially: a San Francisco or London startup selling an AI product into the EU market is caught. But there are carve-outs. Military, defence, and national-security AI systems are excluded entirely. AI used purely for personal, non-professional activity is out. Research and development activity that never reaches the market is out, though the moment a research output becomes a product, scope snaps in. Open-source AI is partially carved out, but not entirely: the free-and-open-source exclusion only applies when the model carries no monetisation, no service wrapping, and no systemic-risk classification under Article 51. The Act also excludes AI systems already regulated by sector-specific EU law (aviation, medical devices, automotive) where those regulations impose equivalent requirements — but only for the overlapping parts. Third-country law-enforcement use is excluded unless there is an international agreement in place. The practical timeline: from February 2025 the prohibited-practices ban took effect; from August 2026 the high-risk and GPAI obligations become enforceable. As of September 2026, anyone shipping an AI system into the EU market must already have a conformity assessment path mapped, because the grace period ended on 2 August 2026. The scope question is not academic — it determines whether you need a notified body, a CE mark, a risk-management system, and human-oversight documentation, or whether you can watch from the sidelines.
